o: Recall the essential ideas of algorithm design and flowcharts.
c: An algorithm must be finite, precise and able to produce an intended result for allowed inputs.
Use terminal (start/end), process (rectangle), input/output (parallelogram), decision (diamond) and labelled arrows.
A decision directs execution along yes/no paths; an invalid input can loop back to the input step.
Trace both representations on the same input to check they perform the same actions.

m.title: Algorithm Design and Flowcharts · worked example
m.q: Design a flowchart that repeatedly asks for a mark until it is between 0 and 100 inclusive. [5 marks]
st: START → input mark using a parallelogram.
Decision checks whether 0 ≤ mark ≤ 100; YES continues to END.
NO returns to input mark, rather than ending; label both arrows. [5]

w: Write the steps for an algorithm that asks for an age until age ≥ 0. [4]
Start/input age [1]; decision age ≥ 0 [1]; valid branch ends/continues [1]; invalid branch loops to input [1].
Explain the difference between a process symbol and decision symbol. [4]
Process is a rectangle [1] representing an operation/calculation [1]; decision is a diamond [1] selecting a path depending on a condition [1].
Trace a validation flowchart when marks entered are -1, 75. [4]
-1 is rejected as below range [1]; arrow loops back [1]; 75 is within 0–100 [1]; flow follows valid branch to end [1].

k.q: Predict whether a value passes a range check.
k.code:
mark = 75
if mark >= 0 AND mark <= 100 then
    print("Valid")
else
    print("Try again")
endif
p: Extend to detect the special boundary value 100.
k.a: Valid; then Try again; 100 should also be accepted because <= includes the upper boundary.
